items.title: John Handy Interview, 1963-11-21
items.q: he said for me to come up there... So we talked it over and they offered me $115 a week for the century. So I took the job. I went on up there and played at that Democratic Club. I stayed up there with them about a year or something.

ctx.x: Did they have your name up? You know, did they advertise you were playing there as guest artist? No. No.

No, they didn't even advertise. Not as I can remember. But anyway, uh, this guy, Charlie Crest was playing, uh, accordion with Faith, the us at that time. And, uh, he got back to St. Louis. He had his own band. And, uh, he said for me to come up there, but I didn't go that time. Uh, because I had too much work in the owners. I couldn't leave. I mean, I had too many contracts signed. I couldn't leave. So, uh, so about six, eight months after he come down here, with Faith again, and the farm and then told me he had…
What did you, uh, you got any questions?
